channel.title: RSS Aggregator Feed
channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: YouTube digs deeper into AI, changing your homepage and how videos are made, but exec says, 'we only succeed when creators succeed'
item.description: YouTube is rolling out a huge collection of Gemini AI-powered tools that will enhance the homepage for viewers and video editing and presentation tools for creators.

item.title: Enveda secures $311M to bring more nature-derived AI drugs into clinical trials
item.description: The round valued the AI biotech at $2 billion. It is currently testing drugs that treat skin conditions and preserve weight loss after stopping GLP-1s.

item.title: Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 platform could herald the age of camera-equipped earbuds — but are we ready for that?
item.description: The new Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 chipset could herald the age of camera-equipped earbuds, but Qualcomm promises ‘this isn’t about putting a chatbot in your ear’.

item.title: The new Beats 360 are 'some of the most comfortable, best-sounding headphones' — and you can save a whopping 80% on an extra pair of earcups
item.description: The Beats 360 headphones were just released yesterday, and Amazon already has an impressive 80% discount on its colorful Cushion Kit.

item.title: Modal Motors is trying to cut China out of electric motors entirely
item.description: The startup is working on small, light motors with no rare-earth magnets that are suited for drones, fans, and robots.

item.title: Interpol uses AI to identify 126 terrorists by analyzing over 100,000 images with new facial recognition tools
item.description: Interpol says the AI's real job was decluttering the stack to 6,362 for a face matcher launched in 2016.

item.title: Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
item.description: Modern life comes with an unending, auto-populating to-do list. It never ceases to amaze me how I can be doing nothing at all, minding my own business, and suddenly something needs to be taken care of. You're telling me a tree branch fell in the backyard and now I have to figure out what to […]

item.title: Spotify is giving you the keys to its algorithm. Here’s how to change what it recommends
item.description: Spotify’s new Taste Profile lets listeners use everyday language to ask for more or less of certain artists, genres and vibes. Spotify is aiming to personalize your user profile more than ever before.

item.title: Most workers are working on Sundays—here’s why
item.description: The trend is more common among younger generations, with 76% of Gen Z workers and 62% of millennials saying they often work on Sunday. Nearly three-quarters of workers (74%) work on Sunday, including 21% who work a full or near-full day, according to Owl Labs’ tenth annual State of Hybrid Work report.

item.title: The GMKtec M8 is a surprisingly powerful 4.5-star mini PC for the office — and it's now discounted at Amazon
item.description: GMKtec's M8 mini PC impressed during testing, smoothly tackling every day-to-day office task we threw at it. And Amazon has dropped the price in the US and UK.

item.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
item.description: A clandestine card-counting operation suggests we may need new ways to spot agent-to-agent deception.

item.title: Raising kids in the age of AI? Technology that fosters connection is more important than ever
item.description: Speaking at the Fast Company Innovation Festival, a panel of experts shared how parents can navigate tech and prepare their kids for the future. Not so long ago, parents debated how much TV time to allow their children.

item.title: How the Epstein files became a focus of Ohio’s Senate race
item.description: In Ohio, the Epstein issue continues to anger—and divide—voters across the political spectrum. Billionaire Les Wexner has long been a magnet for political campaigns seeking contributions—especially in his native Ohio, where the retail tycoon directed a generous portion of his giving to candidates from both parties. Then came the Epstein files.

item.title: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a slate of bills on Monday that could finally give communities better data - and more say - on how data centers impact their electricity bills and water supply. As data centers invade a growing number of communities across the US, they've triggered protests over how the infrastructure underpinning AI […]

item.title: Why diesel prices are so high and what it could mean for the cost of living
item.description: When the cost of fueling up a tractor on a farm goes up by 77%, the cost of the goods that farm produces are going to rise as well. Diesel is the talk of the town, and for good reason: Prices of diesel fuel are at record highs in the United States, recently reaching an average of $6.53 per gallon.

item.title: Bentley Wants Its Torcal SUV to Break the Curse of the Luxury EV
item.description: The British high-end auto company reveals its first-ever full EV: 330 miles of range, 0 to 60 mph in under 3 seconds, and an orchestra under the hood. Will it be enough to lure high-rollers?

item.title: Disney+ and Hulu add to the growing trend of streaming inflation
item.description: At the same time, Disney appears to be exploring new ways to expand its streaming business beyond simply raising subscription prices.

item.title: These popular TP-Link home security cameras could be hacked to spy on you while you sleep, experts warn
item.description: A passwordless login bypass in TP-Link's Tapo C200 and C120 cameras can expose your live feed to anyone on the same network, and a fix is already available to download

item.title: The Pope’s AI Guy Is Worried About ‘Cartel’ Behavior Among Big Labs
item.description: Paolo Benanti tells WIRED that hysteria over whether godlike AI could destroy humanity is distracting from the need for public debate about how to govern the technology.
